title: Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad equation in different bases: application to driven-dissipative two- and multilevel systems
authors: O. A. Ilinskaya, O. V. Ivakhnenko, A. I. Ryzhov, O. Yu. Kitsenko, S. N. Shevchenko
abstract: An open quantum system can be described by a master equation, of which one of the most popular is the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. We revisit description of driven-dissipative quantum systems focusing on the appropriate choice of the system's basis and the respective transformations. We consider the GKSL equation in different bases and calculate the dynamics for a qubit and for a qudit. An appropriate choice of the basis is a fundamental problem for theoretical consideration of open quantum systems and provides an opportunity to obtain the desired evolution in practice.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical review of describing driven-dissipative quantum systems using the GKSL master equation. It argues that the choice of basis (e.g., diabatic vs. instantaneous eigenbasis) is critical, as it dictates the correct mathematical form of the evolution equations. By analyzing multiple bases for qubit and qudit systems, the authors provide necessary guidelines for theorists modeling complex open quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the correct mathematical basis for formulating the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation when describing driven-dissipative quantum systems.
main_result: The choice of basis—such as diabatic, instantaneous eigenbasis, or Floquet basis—fundamentally dictates the correct form of the master equation and its associated Hamiltonian terms, especially near avoided crossings.
method: The authors analyze the GKSL equation by transforming operators and Hamiltonians between various bases (e.g., using transfer matrices) to ensure physical consistency across different dynamical regimes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on driven-dissipative two- and multilevel quantum systems, exemplified initially by a qubit governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$. The dynamics are described by the GKSL master equation.
key_observables: Dynamics of the density matrix $ho$, stationary states (interferograms), and transition probabilities related to Landau-Zener tunneling.
important_parameters: Driving parameters ($\Delta, \epsilon(t)$), relaxation rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_\phi$), and adiabaticity parameters ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Born, Markov, and secular approximations for deriving the master equation, and specific assumptions are made regarding the validity of basis transformations in different limits.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates energy level diagrams (diabatic, instantaneous, superadiabatic, Floquet) as a function of detuning $\epsilon_0$, while Table I summarizes properties of these various bases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically revisits the GKSL equation derivation, analyzes its application to time-dependent Hamiltonians in multiple bases (diabatic vs. instantaneous), and discusses advanced techniques like superadiabatic and Floquet formulations for periodically driven systems.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles a fundamental theoretical challenge: ensuring that the mathematical description of open quantum dynamics remains physically consistent regardless of the chosen computational basis, which is crucial for accurate modeling in quantum optics and superconducting circuits.
